backtest.note: Published Strategy Tester reports — backtests, not live trading. XM Global (Real 2), 30 Dec 2024 – 11 Nov 2025: net profit $38,425 on a $1,000 deposit, profit factor 10.61, maximal drawdown 34.32%, 396 trades (318 won), modelling quality 63.20% with 4 mismatched-chart errors. The second published run, FBS (Real 3), 10 Jun 2024 – 2 Dec 2025, shows $164,642 on a $3,500 deposit at profit factor 21.72 and 21.31% maximal drawdown, on 90.00% modelling quality. Both take effectively one side of gold — 393 of the XM run's 396 trades and all 349 of the FBS run's were long. Low modelling quality and mismatched bars can flatter a system, so read these as historical simulations rather than evidence of live results.

verification.report: Both runs were on gold with every-tick modelling, and both are long-only in effect — the system buys XAUUSD and holds through the trend. That is the shape to understand before buying: the equity curve depends on gold making progress over the test window, and the FBS curve shows it plainly, sitting nearly flat for months before stepping up sharply on a handful of trades (its two largest wins are $39,979 and within consecutive runs of $79,185). The XM run's 63.20% modelling quality is below the 90% that makes an M30 backtest trustworthy, and it logged 4 mismatched-chart errors, so its 10.61 profit factor should be treated as optimistic. Nothing here has been forward-tested on a tracked account.

backtest.note: Published Strategy Tester report — a backtest, not live trading. FBS (Real 9), 7 Sep – 8 Dec 2021, every tick on M15 EURUSD: net profit $9,941 on a $1,000 deposit, profit factor 1.91, maximal drawdown $8,406 (46.80%), 1,867 trades of which 1,343 won. Modelling quality was 87.18% with 28 mismatched-chart errors, both of which are below the standard that makes a backtest trustworthy. Every one of the 1,867 trades was a short — the report is titled "FXCore100 SELL" and shows no long positions. Two things to weigh against the headline profit: the product recommends H4 while this test ran M15, and the product's own money-management table puts M15 accounts in the $11,000–$16,000 bracket, not $1,000. Treat these as historical simulations, not evidence of live results.

verification.report: FXCore100 is a grid seller on EURUSD: the report takes 1,867 short trades and no longs, adding positions as price rises against the entry and closing them as it retraces. That is what produces a rising curve at a 71.9% win rate — and also the 46.80% maximal drawdown, because the losing 28% of trades are held through as the grid widens. The drawdown is the number to focus on: on a $1,000 account it means roughly half the equity was at risk at the worst point of the test, on a timeframe the product itself says needs eleven to sixteen thousand to run at low risk. Nothing here has been forward-tested on a tracked account.
